ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure there is a vertical insulating support rod, with small ball A fixed at the top; the bottom end of the support rod is near the horizontal ground and the starting point of the inclined plane. On the right side is a smooth insulating inclined plane slanting upward to the right, and the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal plane is marked as 30°, with small ball B at rest on the inclined plane. The figure and the meaning of the problem indicate that B and A are at the same height. Then reason: The length of the support rod is 10 cm, so the vertical height of A from the bottom end of the inclined plane is h=10 cm. B is on an inclined plane with inclination angle 30° and is at the same height as A, therefore the distance of B along the inclined plane is s=h/sin30°=10 cm/(1/2)=20 cm. The horizontal distance of B relative to A is r=s cos30°=20 cm×(√3/2)=10√3 cm=0.1√3 m. Since A and B are at the same height and carry equal amounts of the same kind of charge, the Coulomb repulsive force of A on B is horizontally to the right. For B, force balance along the direction of the inclined plane: the component of the Coulomb force upward along the inclined plane is F_e cos30°, and the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sin30°, so F_e cos30°=mg sin30°, that is F_e=mg tan30°. The mass of B is m=30√3 g=0.03√3 kg, g=10 m/s², so mg=0.3√3 N, F_e=0.3√3×(1/√3)=0.3 N. From Coulomb's law F_e=kq²/r², take k=9×10^9 N·m²/C², r=0.1√3 m, then q=sqrt(F_e r²/k)=sqrt[0.3×(0.1√3)²/(9×10^9)]=sqrt[0.3×0.03/(9×10^9)]=sqrt(1.0×10^-12)=1.0×10^-6 C.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: A is at the top of a vertical insulating rod on the left, the rod foot is at the bottom of a smooth incline, the incline makes 30° with the horizontal, and B lies on the incline to the right at the same height as A. From the text, take the rod height as 10 cm, equal like charges on A and B, mass of B as 30√3 g, and g=10 m/s². Use the image/text height relation to compute B’s position: since B is 10 cm above the base on a 30° incline, its distance along the incline is 10/sin30° = 20 cm, so its horizontal separation from A is 20cos30° = 10√3 cm. Because A and B are at the same height, the electrostatic repulsion on B is horizontal. For equilibrium on the smooth incline, resolve forces along the incline: the component of electric force up the plane is F_e cos30°, and the component of weight down the plane is mg sin30°. Set F_e cos30° = mg sin30°, so F_e = mg tan30°. Then apply Coulomb’s law F_e = kq²/r² with r = 10√3 cm and k = 9×10^9 N·m²/C² to solve q = 1.0×10^-6 C.

The horizontal distance of B relative to A is r=s cos30°=20 cm×(√3/2)=10√3 cm=0.1√3 m.
